rounds.text: Aequs Ltd exhibits explosive top-line momentum, evidenced by a 49% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a 15% compounded sales growth over 3 years [E13, E14]. This revenue acceleration is reinforced by screen reasons highlighting strong sales growth with sales up 45% year-over-year alongside sequential quarterly improvements [E51, E52, E54]. Institutional confidence is actively building, demonstrated by foreign institutions increasing their stake to 5.93% from 4.05% and driving a positive overall institutional money flow [E31, E33]. The company is also showing positive operational momentum, being flagged as expected to give a good quarter with profit up quarter-on-quarter [E43, E53]. On the market front, the stock displays resilient technical health with a solid relative-strength rating of 72 against the Nifty 500 and a respectable Sharpe ratio of 1.12 [E37, E40]. Conceded: the business currently struggles with negative profitability metrics, low return on equity, and high valuation multiples including a 10.19x price-to-book ratio [E1, E8, E16].

Aequs Ltd trades at an extreme valuation that completely detaches from its underlying fundamentals, sporting a price-to-book ratio of 10.19x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 116.93x against a sector benchmark of just 12.03x [E10]. Profitability metrics are deeply in the red, evidenced by an ROE of -10.0% [E12], an ROA of -6.33% [E7], and compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months plunging by -311% [E16]. Operational efficiency is also deteriorating rapidly, with operating margins collapsing by 9 percentage points over three years to 4% in the TTM [E19] alongside rising debtor days from 64.0 to 78.5 days [E49] and a low interest coverage ratio [E45]. Furthermore, cash generation is severely compromised: operating cash flow hit negative Rs 99 Cr [E24] and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs 440 Cr [E28] in Mar 2026, while borrowings climbed to Rs 836 Cr [E28] and promoters pledged 25.4% of their holdings [E47]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong top-line momentum with 49% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E14] and positive institutional money flow [E33].

Conceded: [E1], [E10], [E12], [E7], [E16], [E19], [E49], [E45], [E24], [E28], and [E47]. While those fundamental headwinds are real, the bear ignores the aggressive growth phase that justifies upfront capital deployment, evidenced by a massive 49% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and 15% over three years [E13, E14]. This top-line acceleration is translating into tangible operational catalysts, including positive institutional money flow with foreign institutions increasing their stake by 1.88 percentage points [E31, E33]. The company is actively investing in its future capacity, demonstrated by capital-work-in-progress jumping 57.0% to Rs 124 Cr, directly supporting expectations for a good upcoming quarter [E29, E43]. Furthermore, the market price remains resilient above its 200-day moving average with a solid relative-strength rating of 72 against the Nifty 500 and a healthy Sharpe ratio of 1.12, reflecting strong underlying accumulation by smart money despite near-term earnings noise [E36, E37, E40].

Conceded: sales growth is strong at 49% TTM [E14], but this top-line expansion has failed to generate value as compounded profit growth plummeted -311% over the same period [E16]. While foreign institutions increased their stake [E31] and money flow is positive [E33], domestic institutions significantly reduced theirs by 2.35 percentage points [E32], and these shifts cannot mask a negative ROE of -10% [E12, E56]. The bull's focus on capital-work-in-progress [E29] ignores that this expansion is fueled by rising borrowings of Rs 836 Cr [E28] while the company's ROCE of 1.29% remains drastically lower than the sector median of 13.4% [E9, E61]. Technical indicators like the Sharpe ratio [E40] and relative strength [E37] are undermined by extreme annualised volatility of 52.1% [E39] and a P/E of -86.54x [E5]. Finally, the expectation of a good quarter [E43] is contradicted by a decreasing operating-margin trend over four years [E21] and negative free cash flow of Rs -440 Cr [E25].
